# /discipline — what this lane's method obligations are, and what is outstanding

Thin macro over the **already-coded** `tools.discipline` checker. Do NOT re-implement the owed-set
computation, the record validation, or the phase ordering — `tools/discipline/check.py` encodes all
three, `harness/risk-policy.toml` declares which lane owes what, and `harness/disciplines.toml`
declares what each discipline is.

## Run the checker

`$ARGUMENTS` is passed **positionally** to the module — the task packet directory, optionally with
`--phase`:

!`uv run python -m tools.discipline $ARGUMENTS`

With no `--phase`, the packet's current `state.json` phase is used.

## Route on the exit code

| Exit | Meaning | What to do |
|------|---------|------------|
| 0 | every owed discipline is validly discharged | nothing; the transition will not be refused for this reason |
| 1 | at least one is missing or its record is defective | **do the discipline**, then record it — see below |
| 3 | the declaration, the policy, or the packet is invalid | fix the declaration or the packet. Do not "do the discipline"; the checker could not decide what is owed |

## When something is outstanding

Read the named skill and follow it — `clarify`, `test-driven-change`, `diagnose`,
`domain-modeling`, `adversarial-review-panel`. The record is written **after** the work, and it must
cite outputs that exist; a record whose outputs are absent is rejected, which is deliberate. The
report prints the first defect per record, so a rejected record tells you what is wrong with it
rather than only that it is wrong.

This command never writes a record. Writing one is a claim that the method was followed, and a tool
that manufactures that claim would turn the discipline back into the checkbox this milestone exists
to stop shipping.

## Where the refusal actually happens

`tools.task_control` — `transition()` refuses with `missing required disciplines: …` before any
state is written, and `phase-gate` reports `discipline: <id>` as a refresh reason so a resumed
session is refused too. This command is the read-only view of the same computation, not a second
gate.
